newsitem.title: ITALY: Soccer-Vicenza becomes Italy's first foreign-owned club.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Vicenza becomes Italy's first foreign-owned club.

text.p: Serie A side Vicenza became Italy's first foreign-owned soccer club on Friday when it was sold by auction to a British investment company in a bankruptcy court.

The Stellican company's lone bid, worth 22.75 billion lire ($13.5 million), was accepted by judge Magda Cristiano after two potential rivals, both Italian and one a consortium of local businesses, dropped out of the race.
Only Stellican representatives were in court.
Vicenza, who were promoted to serie A in 1995, have qualified for next season's European Cup Winners' Cup.
Based in the affluent northeast city of Vicenza, the club has a profitable balance sheet but was put into receivership as a result of bankruptcy affecting the owners.

City mayor Marino Quaresimin, who had previously expressed a preference for continued local ownership, gave a cautious welcome to Stellican, saying contacts with the company suggested that it was well-intentioned.
"I hope the English company can construct a medium and long-term programme to ensure Vicenza stays competitive," Quaresimin told Reuters.
"Soccer is very important in our city and our fans are very attentive and very passionate," the mayor said.
"I hope they (Stellican) don't underestimate the fact that as of now Vicenza is the only club in the hands of a foreign company," he added, implying that the experiment would be closely watched.
The club itself was non-committal on its new owners in a statement issued by director general Sergio Gasparin.
"All I can do is take note of the decision reached by the Milan court," Gasparin said.

"I am waiting to talk to the managing director of Stellican, Stephen Julius, in order to make an overall judgment and to understand the specifics of the programme which the British group intends to pursue," he said.
Stellican, closely linked to U.S. investment group Apollo, specialises in buying distressed companies, according to British media reports.

Julius told the London Financial Times on Wednesday that his group wanted to redevelop Vicenza's ageing Romeo Menti stadium, which the club leases from the city council, invest in new players and develop sponsorship and merchandising.
He added, however, that he was worried that a foreign takeover would prove unpopular with local fans.
